rows.title: A Flour-Filled Afternoon
rows.story: Last summer, I visited my grandmother in Lisbon, and we spent a lovely afternoon baking an apple pie together. The kitchen was filled with the warm scent of cinnamon and the soft hum of the oven. As I stirred the mixture, I accidentally spilled a handful of flour across the kitchen floor. My grandmother laughed, her eyes twinkling with joy. In that moment, I felt an overwhelming sense of gratitude for the simple, heartfelt connection we shared.

rows.title: The Day I Felt the Wind
rows.story: I was seven years old when my dad taught me to ride a bike. It was a red bike we bought at a garage sale, and I remember the excitement of getting it. We practiced in the church parking lot on Sundays, and I fell down so many times that I almost lost hope. But one day, he let go, and I didn't even notice. I just kept going, feeling the wind in my hair and the thrill of freedom.

rows.title: A Friday Ritual
rows.story: When we moved to Austin in 2019, we didn’t know anyone. My wife Priya found this taco place on South Congress, and we basically went there every Friday for a year. The owner, Luis, started remembering our order. That’s kind of when it started to feel like home.

rows.title: A Moment of Relief
rows.story: I remember checking my exam results on my phone at the bus stop. I passed. I passed the bar exam on the second try. The moment I saw the word 'passed' on the screen, my heart swelled with relief. I called my mom right away, and before I even finished the sentence, she started crying. Her tears made me feel seen, supported, and deeply loved.

rows.title: Biscuit's Couch
rows.story: We adopted Biscuit from the shelter in March. He was scared of everything—like the vacuum, the doorbell, even his own reflection. At first, he would hide behind the furniture, trembling whenever there was a sudden noise. It took him about three weeks before he would sleep on the couch with us. Now he won't get off it. He's found his place, and we've found ours.

rows.title: Candlelight and Cards
rows.story: During the ice storm, there was a power outage that lasted two days. With no electricity, the house fell into a quiet stillness, broken only by the occasional creak of the roof and the sound of wind howling against the windows. My brother and I decided to pass the time by playing cards by candlelight, mostly gin rummy. He won every single game, and even now, years later, he still brings it up with a grin. It was a simple moment, but it felt like a small victory in the face of the storm.

rows.title: The Staff Recommendation Shelf
rows.story: My first job was at a bookstore in Portland called Page Turners. I was sixteen, and the manager, Denise, let me pick the staff recommendation shelf. Every single month, I put Dune on it. It was my way of sharing the book I loved, and it made me feel like I was part of something bigger than myself.

rows.title: The Weight of Hope
rows.story: The night my daughter was born, I remember the nurse handing her to me. I was terrified I would drop her. She was six pounds two ounces. My wife fell asleep right after, and I just sat there holding her until the sun came up.

rows.title: A Finish Line Moment
rows.story: I ran the Chicago marathon in 2022. My knee started hurting around mile eighteen, and I had to walk a lot of the last part. Despite the pain, I pushed through and finished in five hours and twelve minutes. As I crossed the finish line, my sister was there waiting with a sign that read 'You did it!' Her presence brought a wave of joy and contentment, reminding me of the love and support that carried me through the race.
